programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha rudeigin air tuiteam bhon chraoibh – ubhal a th’ ann! Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean ag ionnsachadh g’ eil an t-ubhal a' toirt tòrr toileachais do mhòran. Something has fallen from the tree - it’s an apple! Daolag- bhreac and Seillean learn that the apple gives a lot of happiness to many.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: AChan fhaigh Oona cadal 's i iomagaineach mu bhith seinn aig briseadh an là son a' chiad turas. Tha Mama ga toirt air turas dàna a tha luma làn ceòl gus am faigh an dithis aca òran sònraichte ionnsachadh 's an guthan seinn a' lo. Oona can't sleep for worrying about participating in the dawn chorus for the first time. Mama takes her on a late-night adventure filled with music so that they can learn a special new song together and find their best singing voices.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha an t-acras uabhasach air Baba 's tha bhrù aige rùchdail! Ge-tà, chan eil sgeul air Oona son a thoirt dhachaigh gu bhiadh... an tig aig a bhuthaid bheag dàna a shlighe fhèin a dhèanamh air ais chun an fhaiche? Baba is a hungry puffling and his tummy is very rumbly! However, Oona has gone out to play and isn't around to take him home for dinner. Will the adventurous Baba be able to make his own way back to the puffin burrow?

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha e cho sgarrachail a-muigh an-diugh. Tha Fuigheag cho aotrom – tha e fortanach nach eil e a’ falbh leis a’ ghaoith! It’s gusty out there today. Fuigheag is so light, he’s fortunate that he’s not blown away by the wind!

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha latha math iasgaich aig na Losgannan agus iad a’ glacadh rud ris nach eil dùil! The Froglets enjoy a fin-tastic fishing adventure, ending up with an unexpected catch!

programme.title: Dòtaman
programme.desc: Anns a' prògram tasglainn dhaiteach seo de Dhòtaman tha sinn a' coimhead ri rudan a' fàs anns a' ghàradh ann an cuideachd Dhonnie, Chatriona agus Iain. Tha ceòl is òran, sgeulachd is cluiche gu leòr ri fhaotainn agus feuch gun coimhead sibh airson Cagnaidh is Crotal, agus gum bi sibh deiseal airson Nelson is Napoleon aig a' ghleoc! In this archive edition of Dotaman, Donnie, Cathy and John explore the fun of growing things in the garden, with music, song and lots of activity to enjoy. Look out for Cagnaidh and Crotal and join Nelson and Napoleon to tell the time at the Dotaman clock.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leughadh An Sligeanach as Luaithe sa Bhaile. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Howard Calvert, a dhealbhachadh le Karen Obuhanych agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Joy Dunlop reads An Sligeanach as Luaithe sa Bhaile by Howard Calvert, illustrated by Karen Obuhanych and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Stella a’ cur speuchlairean oirre 'son coimhead nas glice – mar Mia agus Stella, chan eil rudan ag obrachadh a-mach mar a tha i a' lùiginn! When Stella puts glasses on to appear more intelligent, like Mia, things don’t work out as she had hoped!

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Molaidh na boil’ nuair a tha i fhèin is Stella a' dol a-mach air Oidhche Shamhna. Tha Stella a’ dèanamh a-mach gu bheil i ro shean air a shon - ach an dùil a’ bheil sin fìor? Molaidh is really excited when she and Stella go out trick or treating. Stella makes out she is too old for Halloween, but is this really true?

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha Mgr Mackle fo uallach agus chan eil e a’ faighinn fois an àite sam bith. Tha Ms Dallas air a dòigh glan gu bheil An Còirneal Cliseam a' tadhal air an sgoil airson clas air leth a theagaisg. Mr Mackle is under pressure and he can't seem to get any respite. Ms Dallas is delighted that Colonel Clisham is visiting the school to teach a camouflage class.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Às deidh do Bhonns a bhith cho gionnach air Là Blàth-chnuimh’s gu bheil i air a h-uile cnuimh a bh’ann ithe, tha i a' ròghnachadh flùr blàth-chnuimh a ghoid 'o na Bògaisean gus am faigh Uilidh air blàth-chnuimh a bhlaiseadh cuideachd. When Bonns is so greedy that she eats all the grubs on Grubloom Day, she must retrieve some grubloom flowers from the Bògaisean so that Uilidh can taste a grubloom, too.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha na càraidean a' trod le chèile, tha a h-uile cail a th’ ann a’ dol bun-os-cionn aig a' Ghumbal-railidh. Ach airson fuasgladh fhaighinn, feumaidh na càraidean tighinn gu rèite airson an latha a shàbhaladh! When the twins fall out with one another, everything goes topsy turvy at the Gumbal-railidh. To solve the situation, the twins must reconcile and save the day!

programme.title: Fuine
programme.desc: Gregor makes chewy and salty bread pretzels that are the perfect snack or lunchbox filler. Griogar MacLeòid is eileanaich eile lem molaidhean son fuine bhlasta staigh agaibh pfhèin

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: We meet Gaelic learner Ben Geyer from Fife and Calum Maclean is in St Monans, finding out about the prosperity white gold brought to the area.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts a new quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams from winning are the Pretenders, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Marcas and Morvyn or Fraoch and Raibeart, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Marcas & Morvyn no Fraoch & Raibeart, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Aithris le Darren Linc a chaidh a chraoladh lathaichean mus an do bhòt an Rìoghachd Aonaichte airson Brexit ann an 2016. Darren Laing’s 2016 report, first broadcast days before the United Kingdom’s vote to leave the European Union.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Turas fèin-aithne dha boireannach Dhubh tar-ghnèitheach ann am Brasil. A journey of self-discovery for a black trans woman in Brazil.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Prògram aithriseach ciùil le Julie Fowlis is Muireann NicAmhlaoibh 's iad air slighe rannsachaidh mu na freumhan aca fhèin. Nì iadsan siubhal thar chrìochan 's thar chleachdaidhean eadar taobh siar na h-Èirinn agus Eileanan Siar na h-Alba, a' coinneachadh, a' conaltradh 's a' cluich ciùil air an t-slighe. Chì sinn Julie agus Muireann ann an caochladh àiteachan a tha ainmeil airson òrain, ceòl agus beul-aithris agus a' feitheamh airson fàilte chridheil a chur orra, tha eòlaichean ciùil, pìobairean agus seinneadairean. Anns a' phrògram seo chì sinn stuth nach fhacas a-riamh à Alba agus Èirinn. Musical documentary presented by Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh in which they explore their shared musical heritage. Julie and Muireann cross borders and traditions from the Western Isles to the west coast of Ireland, meeting and making music en route. They visit several locations that are synonymous with folk song, music and folklore. Welcoming them to each destination are musicians, pipers and singers, and this episode features previously unseen footage from both Scotland and Ireland.

programme.title: Na h-Eileanaich: Barra and Vatersay
programme.desc: Barra and Vatersay are often perceived as being just a tourist destination. But a closer look reveals a strong, thriving community not solely dependent on tourism, even without the infrastructure and conveniences of the mainland. This programme shows not only the fragility of a living community but also the determination and robustness of the people within. Thathas tric a’ faicinn Barraigh agus Bhatarsaigh dìreach àite turasachd. Ach, eadhon às aonais bun-structair agus goireasan thìr-mhòir, nuair a choimheadas tu nas mionaidiche, tha coimhearsnachd làidir is soirbheachail ann nach eil a-mhàin steidhichte air turasachd. ’S e program adhartach is sunndach a th’ anns “Na h-Eileanaich” a tha a’ sealltainn, chan e a-mhàin, cho cugalach uaireanan a tha coimhearsnachd bheò, ach cuideachd cho daingeann agus cho neartmhor sa tha a’ choimhearsnachd sin. Le dealbhan àlainn, agallamhan agus guthan-leirigidh, tha sin ga thoirt am follais. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: The Fairy-Tale Castles of King Ludwig II with Dan Cruickshank
programme.desc: Ludwig II of Bavaria, more commonly known by his nicknames the Swan King or the Dream King, is a legendary figure - the handsome boy-king, loved by his people, betrayed by his cabinet and found dead in tragic and mysterious circumstances. He spent his life in pursuit of the ideal of beauty, which found expression in three of the most extraordinary, ornate architectural schemes imaginable - the castle of Neuschwanstein and the palaces of Linderhof and Herrenchiemsee. Today, these three buildings are among Germany's biggest tourist attractions. In this documentary, Dan Cruickshank explores the rich aesthetic of Ludwig II - from the mock-medievalism of Neuschwanstein, the iconic fairy-tale castle that became the inspiration for the one in Walt Disney's Sleeping Beauty, to the rich, baroque splendour of Herrenchiemsee, Ludwig's answer to Versailles. Dan argues that Ludwig's castles are more than flamboyant kitsch and are, in fact, the key to unravelling the eternal enigma of Ludwig II.

programme.title: A Year in the Wild
programme.desc: The harsh beauty and surprising wildlife of Scotland's Cairngorms National Park through the eyes of the people who know it best. The Cairngorms is Britain's largest and wildest National Park. A land of Arctic extremes in the heart of the Scottish highlands. Its granite mountains and ancient pine forests are home to some of our rarest and most spectacular animals, including golden eagles, ptarmigan, capercaillie, red deer and crested tits. This lyrical and thought-provoking film reveals the inner secrets of this wild landscape over a year through the eyes of individuals who know and love the Cairngorms: a mountain guide, an artist, a salmon ghillie, a gamekeeper and a nature writer.

programme.title: Atlantic: The Wildest Ocean on Earth
programme.desc: In the balmy tropical Atlantic, everything from dolphins, manatees and whale sharks to sunbathing jellyfish thrive in the Caribbean's warm, sheltered waters, fringed with coral reefs and rich mangrove forests. But extreme heat in Africa unleashes terrifying hurricanes, causing chaos across the region.

programme.title: Art of Spain
programme.desc: Critic and art historian Andrew Graham-Dixon travels from southern to northern Spain to tell the story of some of Europe's most exciting and vital art. For 700 years, most of Spain was an Islamic state, and the south was its beating heart. Under the Moors, Spain became the most advanced, wealthy and populous country in Europe. Andrew travels to Cordoba, Seville and Granada, visiting beautiful Moorish palaces and mosques, telling the story of one of the most colourful and sophisticated cultures to ever appear in Europe.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Broadcaster and writer Sally Magnusson takes her seat in the original, imposing Mastermind chair, and shares memories of her father Magnus's time as the host of one of British television's most enduring quiz shows. She tells the story of how the programme originated, how her father got the job of quiz master, and what it was like growing up as a teenager and having the catchphrases 'pass' and 'I've started, so I'll finish' hurled your way on a regular basis. Sally also reveals how it feels to sit and face questions in the famous chair and how it came to be that it now lives in her own living room as, literally, part of the furniture.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the 1972 final of the classic quiz.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson chairs as Arthur Marshall, Sally Magnusson and Peter Egan take on Frank Muir, Anna Massey and Godfrey Smith in the panel game of word definitions and deceptions.

programme.title: Becoming Frida Kahlo
programme.desc: Dangerous politics and turbulent love shock Frida's world. After conducting a short affair with Leon Trotsky, Diego's political mentor, she finally achieves her own solo exhibition in Europe. But all does not go according to plan, and she returns to Mexico to find that Diego wants a divorce. Pouring her pain into work, she creates one of her most famous masterpieces - The Two Fridas. After an assassination and an arrest, Diego and Frida are reunited in San Francisco. But her health problems increase, and she spends her last years in excruciating pain, continuing to paint all the while and creating some of her most enduring and heartbreaking images.

programme.title: Turner: The Man Who Painted Britain
programme.desc: While Joseph Mallord William Turner is considered by many to be Britain's greatest landscape painter, his private life reveals a man of extremes and contradictions. This docudrama explores the extraordinary story of a brilliant self-made man.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The Economist's interview with Elon Musk attracted global attention before Musk then described interviewer Zanny Minton Beddoes as a 'traitor to the West'. The interview followed 90 minutes of conversation for The Insider, The Economist's video series. Zanny Minton Beddoes, Editor-in-Chief of The Economist, explains how the interview came about and the reaction after it was published. Huge wildfires in France and Spain have dominated news coverage across Europe, creating difficult and sometimes dangerous conditions for journalists reporting from the scene. Sadiya Chowdhury, correspondent at Sky News, explains her approach, and Mehdi Lebouachera, global director at AFP, gives the backstory to a photograph that appeared on front pages around the world.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s cause for celebration as the park’s North American tree porcupine has given birth to a precious porcupette, the first to be born here. The keepers are thrilled, but within hours the tiny baby begins exploring the enclosure alone, leaving mum behind. Keepers must work fast to keep this bold adventurer safe. Meanwhile, Kate catches up with Malaika, the elderly lioness who survived a risky sedation and was diagnosed with heart disease. The situation is further complicated by Malaika refusing her medication, but there is a glimmer of hope when the weakened matriarch is accepted back into the pride.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Neil hunts down a stolen Toyota Hilux hidden on a remote industrial estate. But before he can seize it, he’s confronted by a man claiming he bought it at an auction.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A young boy is murdered, but his killer is not found. Thirty years on, a pollen expert finds crucial evidence. And a blood and fibre analyst helps find the killer of a shopworker.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles talks to guitar enthusiast Martin Waugh about his impressive collection of rare and valuable instruments. Martin has gigged with some of the biggest names in pop music, and in this episode, he explains his knowledge and lifelong passion for the electric guitar. There’s even an impromptu rendition of the show's theme tune on his beloved Fender Stratocaster! But there’s no time for an encore, as two teams are ready to go antique-shopping with their experts. In red are friends Ranjit and Paula with Nick Hall. Married couple Kate and Sam are in blue with Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds consider their first possible move – an expensive Victorian games compendium! Meanwhile, Sam gets in a spin over a quirky metal globe, but Izzie thinks it’s a bit dull. At the auction in Etwall, Derbyshire, there’s fighting talk when one expert reckons their team is born to bargain-hunt.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is on patrol at Dunfermline recycling centre, hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. Blacksmith Kev creates a metal masterpiece from obsolete tools, while JJ tries to double the charm of two rattan chairs. JJ hands over a huge profit, but which upcycled find will generate the most cash?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: With the help of Alistair Appleton, a couple want to escape land-locked life in a Leicestershire town and relocate to a county with a coastline. So, they’ve decided to make a new life for themselves in either Somerset or Devon. Alistair also visits the village of Carhampton, where the apple harvest is in full swing in the community orchard.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: When running a big school, how much discipline is too much? Panorama investigates the academy trust where classrooms are silent and pupils can be sent to detention for looking out of the window. For some, reduced disruption and improved exam results at schools run by the Athena Learning Trust in Devon and Cornwall is proof that the tough approach works. But as Richard Bilton reports, many former teachers, students and their parents say the trust’s strict policies on behaviour have gone too far.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The interceptors take on devious scammers posing as the National Crime Agency, who scare their targets into buying gift cards to prove their identities in a complex set of lies telling them they will be arrested if they don’t comply. With the scam hub team having no luck contacting a man who is being targeted on the phone, the ground interceptors are dispatched to his address. But it’s a huge block of flats – will they be able to find and stop him before he pays out?

programme.desc: Eric Knowles talks to guitar enthusiast Martin Waugh about his impressive collection of rare and valuable instruments. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds consider their first possible move – an expensive Victorian games compendium! Meanwhile, Sam gets in a spin over a quirky metal globe, but Izzie thinks it’s a bit dull. At the auction in Etwall, Derbyshire, there’s fighting talk when one expert reckons their team is born to bargain-hunt.

There’s even an impromptu rendition of the show's theme tune on his beloved Fender Stratocaster! But there’s no time for an encore, as two teams are ready to go antique-shopping with their experts. In red are friends Ranjit and Paula with Nick Hall. Married couple Kate and Sam are in blue with Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds consider their first possible move – an expensive Victorian games compendium! Meanwhile, Sam gets in a spin over a quirky metal globe, but Izzie thinks it’s a bit dull. At the auction in Etwall, Derbyshire, there’s fighting talk when one expert reckons their team is born to bargain-hunt.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is on patrol at Dunfermline recycling centre, hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. Blacksmith Kev creates a metal masterpiece from obsolete tools, while JJ tries to double the charm of two rattan chairs. JJ hands over a huge profit, but which upcycled find will generate the most cash?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: With the help of Alistair Appleton, a couple want to escape land-locked life in a Leicestershire town and relocate to a county with a coastline. So, they’ve decided to make a new life for themselves in either Somerset or Devon. Alistair also visits the village of Carhampton, where the apple harvest is in full swing in the community orchard.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Panorama

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s cause for celebration as the park’s North American tree porcupine has given birth to a precious porcupette, the first to be born here. The keepers are thrilled, but within hours the tiny baby begins exploring the enclosure alone, leaving mum behind. Keepers must work fast to keep this bold adventurer safe. Meanwhile, Kate catches up with Malaika, the elderly lioness who survived a risky sedation and was diagnosed with heart disease. The situation is further complicated by Malaika refusing her medication, but there is a glimmer of hope when the weakened matriarch is accepted back into the pride.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Neil hunts down a stolen Toyota Hilux hidden on a remote industrial estate. But before he can seize it, he’s confronted by a man claiming he bought it at an auction.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A young boy is murdered, but his killer is not found. Thirty years on, a pollen expert finds crucial evidence. And a blood and fibre analyst helps find the killer of a shopworker.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles talks to guitar enthusiast Martin Waugh about his impressive collection of rare and valuable instruments. Martin has gigged with some of the biggest names in pop music, and in this episode, he explains his knowledge and lifelong passion for the electric guitar. There’s even an impromptu rendition of the show's theme tune on his beloved Fender Stratocaster! But there’s no time for an encore, as two teams are ready to go antique-shopping with their experts. In red are friends Ranjit and Paula with Nick Hall. Married couple Kate and Sam are in blue with Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds consider their first possible move – an expensive Victorian games compendium! Meanwhile, Sam gets in a spin over a quirky metal globe, but Izzie thinks it’s a bit dull. At the auction in Etwall, Derbyshire, there’s fighting talk when one expert reckons their team is born to bargain-hunt.

So, they’ve decided to make a new life for themselves in either Somerset or Devon. Alistair also visits the village of Carhampton, where the apple harvest is in full swing in the community orchard.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: The fast-paced, fifty-fifty quiz hosted by Jason Manford is back. In this episode, contestants are faced with choices that include Death in Paradise or Midsomer Murders, Michael Owen or Frank Lampard, and Fame or Fortune. Who can stay calm to win the cash?

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Stephen Mangan. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Peter’s suspicions about Lauren grow. Ross remains determined to help Joel.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: When running a big school, how much discipline is too much? Panorama investigates the academy trust where classrooms are silent and pupils can be sent to detention for looking out of the window. For some, reduced disruption and improved exam results at schools run by the Athena Learning Trust in Devon and Cornwall is proof that the tough approach works. But as Richard Bilton reports, many former teachers, students and their parents say the trust’s strict policies on behaviour have gone too far.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The interceptors take on devious scammers posing as the National Crime Agency, who scare their targets into buying gift cards to prove their identities in a complex set of lies telling them they will be arrested if they don’t comply. With the scam hub team having no luck contacting a man who is being targeted on the phone, the ground interceptors are dispatched to his address. But it’s a huge block of flats – will they be able to find and stop him before he pays out?

programme.title: The Rapture

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s cause for celebration as the park’s North American tree porcupine has given birth to a precious porcupette, the first to be born here. The keepers are thrilled, but within hours the tiny baby begins exploring the enclosure alone, leaving mum behind. Keepers must work fast to keep this bold adventurer safe. Meanwhile, Kate catches up with Malaika, the elderly lioness who survived a risky sedation and was diagnosed with heart disease. The situation is further complicated by Malaika refusing her medication, but there is a glimmer of hope when the weakened matriarch is accepted back into the pride.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Neil hunts down a stolen Toyota Hilux hidden on a remote industrial estate. But before he can seize it, he’s confronted by a man claiming he bought it at an auction.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A young boy is murdered, but his killer is not found. Thirty years on, a pollen expert finds crucial evidence. And a blood and fibre analyst helps find the killer of a shopworker.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles talks to guitar enthusiast Martin Waugh about his impressive collection of rare and valuable instruments. Martin has gigged with some of the biggest names in pop music, and in this episode, he explains his knowledge and lifelong passion for the electric guitar. There’s even an impromptu rendition of the show's theme tune on his beloved Fender Stratocaster! But there’s no time for an encore, as two teams are ready to go antique-shopping with their experts. In red are friends Ranjit and Paula with Nick Hall. Married couple Kate and Sam are in blue with Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds consider their first possible move – an expensive Victorian games compendium! Meanwhile, Sam gets in a spin over a quirky metal globe, but Izzie thinks it’s a bit dull. At the auction in Etwall, Derbyshire, there’s fighting talk when one expert reckons their team is born to bargain-hunt.

programme.desc: There’s cause for celebration as the park’s North American tree porcupine has given birth to a precious porcupette, the first to be born here. The keepers are thrilled, but within hours the tiny baby begins exploring the enclosure alone, leaving mum behind. Keepers must work fast to keep this bold adventurer safe. Meanwhile, Kate catches up with Malaika, the elderly lioness who survived a risky sedation and was diagnosed with heart disease. The situation is further complicated by Malaika refusing her medication, but there is a glimmer of hope when the weakened matriarch is accepted back into the pride.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Neil hunts down a stolen Toyota Hilux hidden on a remote industrial estate. But before he can seize it, he’s confronted by a man claiming he bought it at an auction.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A young boy is murdered, but his killer is not found. Thirty years on, a pollen expert finds crucial evidence. And a blood and fibre analyst helps find the killer of a shopworker.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles talks to guitar enthusiast Martin Waugh about his impressive collection of rare and valuable instruments. Martin has gigged with some of the biggest names in pop music, and in this episode, he explains his knowledge and lifelong passion for the electric guitar. There’s even an impromptu rendition of the show's theme tune on his beloved Fender Stratocaster! But there’s no time for an encore, as two teams are ready to go antique-shopping with their experts. In red are friends Ranjit and Paula with Nick Hall. Married couple Kate and Sam are in blue with Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds consider their first possible move – an expensive Victorian games compendium! Meanwhile, Sam gets in a spin over a quirky metal globe, but Izzie thinks it’s a bit dull. At the auction in Etwall, Derbyshire, there’s fighting talk when one expert reckons their team is born to bargain-hunt.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is on patrol at Dunfermline recycling centre, hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. Blacksmith Kev creates a metal masterpiece from obsolete tools, while JJ tries to double the charm of two rattan chairs. JJ hands over a huge profit, but which upcycled find will generate the most cash?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: With the help of Alistair Appleton, a couple want to escape land-locked life in a Leicestershire town and relocate to a county with a coastline. So, they’ve decided to make a new life for themselves in either Somerset or Devon. Alistair also visits the village of Carhampton, where the apple harvest is in full swing in the community orchard.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: When running a big school, how much discipline is too much? Panorama investigates the academy trust where classrooms are silent and pupils can be sent to detention for looking out of the window. For some, reduced disruption and improved exam results at schools run by the Athena Learning Trust in Devon and Cornwall is proof that the tough approach works. But as Richard Bilton reports, many former teachers, students and their parents say the trust’s strict policies on behaviour have gone too far.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The interceptors take on devious scammers posing as the National Crime Agency, who scare their targets into buying gift cards to prove their identities in a complex set of lies telling them they will be arrested if they don’t comply. With the scam hub team having no luck contacting a man who is being targeted on the phone, the ground interceptors are dispatched to his address. But it’s a huge block of flats – will they be able to find and stop him before he pays out?

programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Stephen Mangan. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC News at Six
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Look North (East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire)
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire.

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: Alex Jones and Roman Kemp bring you the stories that matter from across the country.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Peter’s suspicions about Lauren grow. Ross remains determined to help Joel.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: When running a big school, how much discipline is too much? Panorama investigates the academy trust where classrooms are silent and pupils can be sent to detention for looking out of the window. For some, reduced disruption and improved exam results at schools run by the Athena Learning Trust in Devon and Cornwall is proof that the tough approach works. But as Richard Bilton reports, many former teachers, students and their parents say the trust’s strict policies on behaviour have gone too far.

programme.title: The Big Cases
programme.desc: The chilling story of Hull’s funeral home horror. How an undertaker drowning in debt betrayed hundreds of grieving families. Robert Bush hoarded bodies, sold fake funeral plans and presented families with the ashes of strangers. His shocking crimes went undetected for years. The discovery led to one of the most complex investigations in Humberside Police’s history, with help from the National Crime Agency. At the heart of this are grieving families. In their darkest days, they fought for laws to regulate the funeral industry so that others never suffer their pain - or guilt - again.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs finally meets Anika Drake. New nurse Siobhan raises suspicions at Oxsmith. When Bethany is found injured, Gabs and Rafiq plan her escape. Max pushes Caroline to back Rostyre.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: Look North (East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire)
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire.

programme.title: The Mist
programme.desc: A deadly mist descends upon a small Maine town after a huge storm. A man and his son seek refuge in a supermarket where they have to face not only monsters in the mist but the fear and wrath of the other survivors. Horror film based on a story by Stephen King.

programme.title: Weather for the Week Ahead
programme.desc: Detailed weather forecast.

programme.title: Joins BBC News
programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: In this episode of the world's biggest car programme, Richard Hammond is dropped into the remote, frozen wastes of Canada to test a watch with a built-in emergency beacon. Normally, activating the device would summon a vast international rescue crew, but in Hammond's case, the distress signal is sent directly to Jeremy Clarkson and James May who are disorganised, disinterested and very many miles away. Eventually, the pair get their hands on two machines they believe are suitable for the job and set off on an epic adventure to find their colleague. Also in this show, Clarkson is on the track in the new 471-horsepower Lexus RC F coupe whilst star of The Fall and The X-Files Gillian Anderson tries her hand in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: If you took everything from him, betrayed him, trapped him, and broke both his hearts... how far might the Doctor go? Returning to Gallifrey, the Doctor faces the Time Lords in a struggle that will take him to the end of time itself. Who is the Hybrid? And what is the Doctor's confession?

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall takes to the icy waters of British Columbia in search of the biggest, baddest sea lion in the world. After an unexpected encounter with a killer whale, he heads back to the city on the trail of one smelly contender before trying his hand at becoming a raccoon. Despite immense strength, powerful claws and a fearsome reputation in Canada, there's a surprise in store when Steve tracks down the infamous black bear.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve and the crew are thrown deep in the steamy rainforests of Costa Rica. They are on a mission to find the largest cat in South America - the awesome jaguar. But the jungle is teeming with wildlife - from venomous snakes to squealing frogs - so there is plenty to see along the way. Even after dark the forest is alive with deadly creatures, and down by the river Steve has a battle with a giant, reptilian predator.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 3, and it's time for Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Presenter Sophie Willan, alongside judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young, takes the fight to fast fashion with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. First up, in the Pattern Challenge, it’s another sewing bee first as the sewers are tasked with creating pants from old T-shirts. However, they are not asked to make just one pair - they have to make three. This challenge tests not only their technical skill but also their consistency. Then, Patrick and Esme take a trip to a store of waste destined for landfill to hand-pick the raw materials for the Transformation Challenge. Finally, the sewers get protesting as they make outfits with an environmental message made to measure their models.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May take three V8-engined sports cars on a gruelling 1,600-mile journey through the spectacular landscapes of Patagonia. Along the way, they encounter rough roads, collapsed bridges, broken bones and a cow as they press onwards against the odds in a quest to reach the southernmost city in the world.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May continue in their quest to take three V8-engined sports cars on an epic journey through Patagonia to the southernmost city in the world. Along the way they encounter stunning landscapes, mechanical meltdowns and torturously unpaved roads before a terrifying turn of events brings their adventure to a heart-stopping climax.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Craig Gordon is famous for his resilience and defiance of strikers, coaches, critics and doctors. He has granted BBC cameras unprecedented access to his life over 12 months as, at the age of 42, he makes one last attempt to reach a World Cup. Along the way, we learn about the miracle saves and comebacks from injuries that should have ended his career and that have allowed him to still compete at the top level for so many years. From a prodigy at Hearts to a record breaker in the English Premier League and an invincible at Celtic, Craig Gordon has had a career like no other, but there is one thing still missing - an appearance at a World Cup. To get there, he will have to overcome opposition on the pitch as well as the limitations of his own body as he battles injuries to keep the dream alive. A fascinating insight into the mind of one of Scotland’s most driven athletes.

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy Fury’s comeback begins in the shadow of his toughest year yet. With no ability to plan for the future and struggling with his identity, Tommy is at his lowest point personally and professionally, living alone in a house that was meant to be his and Molly-Mae’s forever home. For the first time, Tommy describes the day that Molly-Mae and Bambi left him and just how low he sank into the depths of alcohol. His role as a father to baby Bambi brings both joy and pressure as he tries to win Molly-Mae back and convince her he is a changed man. After finally getting the medical all-clear to fight again, Tommy and his trainer and father, John, prepare for his return to the ring against MMA fighter Darren Till. Team Fury travel down to London for the press conference, with John promising to be on his best behaviour - but when Till mentions Tommy’s brother Tyson, tensions erupt…

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Pride runs deep in the Fury family - and for Tommy, it’s both a legacy and a burden. As he takes his first tentative steps back into the spotlight, we learn how far his father, John, has gone in the name of protecting the family name - including time behind bars. That same fierce loyalty rears its head when Tommy prepares for his first gym appearance since announcing his comeback. But with fighter Darren Till throwing threats and chaos into the mix, John pulls Tommy out of the fight, unwilling to risk Tommy’s future career. It’s a crushing blow for Tommy, who’s desperate for momentum and purpose. Yet amid the pressure, there’s a flicker of hope - Tommy and Molly-Mae are spotted together on New Year’s Eve, with a kiss that hints at a brighter future.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Ruby and Jodi’s partnership deepens as together they reshape the family, and Ruby starts to banish members of the family from their home.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is in Buckinghamshire, determined to stop quality items being crushed at High Wycombe recycling centre. Three old chairs bring tears to the eyes, furniture upcycler Sarah dreams up a wild new look for a side table, and Jacqui's imagination is on fire as she wrestles a plant stand - but will all three items produce profits for their unsuspecting owners?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Suzie fixes a football from a Scottish Cup final, Chris repairs a magazine from a Japanese POW camp, Geoff restores a pachinko machine, and Rebecca fixes a beautiful Cretan lyra.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Sean Fletcher, Louise Minchin, Chris Washington and Kimberly Wyatt take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay hosts this quiz celebrating the UK and all its quirks. Alongside him, Traitors star Paul Gorton acts as an unreliable guide, leading a daily tour packed with fun, facts and fibs. This week’s celebrity contestants are TV icon Anneka Rice, comedian Shane Todd and Radio 1Xtra DJ Remi Burgz. The week kicks off in Whitby, with a daily winner and scores building up to eventually reveal a weekly champion.

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: It's the sixth leg of the Hairy Bikers' adventure and they have made it as far as southern Europe, Italy to be precise. Starting in Venice, the Bikers have to abandon their bikes in favour of a more elegant form of transport, the gondola, but that doesn't stop them cooking. By the side of a canal, they bake a classic focaccia with rosemary. But it's not long before they are back on the road, making a dash for Turin to help celebrate Italy's 150th birthday. In between, they cook a stromboli (American-style rolled-up pizza) and visit a hazelnut farm to learn the secrets of a certain hazelnut and chocolate spread. But it's off the beaten track that they enjoy the 'real Italy'; a pasta pie on the back streets of Ferrara, catching up with Si's sister who lives in Tuscany, visiting old friends at their weekend retreat for a Tuscan feast and the chance to relive The Italian Job on the rooftop track of the old Fiat factory. World-class food, stunning scenery and fantastic people!

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Peter, now in his twenties, has been rearing Berkshire pigs since he was ten. He last competed at the Staffordshire County Show when he was 14. Having balanced university with work on the family farm in the Peak District, he wants to forge a future in farming. If his prized Berkshire pigs win rosettes in the competition ring, it will be not just recognition for him but also a much-needed boost for the breed, one of the rarest and oldest in the UK. While Peter hopes his pigs don’t give him the runaround, dedicated farming couple Lianne and Mark are working hard to grow their pedigree herd of South Devon cattle on rented land near Leek in Staffordshire. They are focused on giving their cows the ultimate beauty treatment so they shine in the show ring. South Devon cattle may be known as gentle giants, but overnighting at the showground, keeping up their energy levels and performing well in front of the judge are just some of the challenges they face to add more hard-earned rosettes to their collection.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: By invitation of the Lord Mayor of the City of London, the Roadshow visits the Mansion House, where Michael Aspel and the experts find both genuine and fake French art glass, a lock of Nelson's hair passed down from his hairdresser, a hand sculpted by Rodin and a broken plate dug up on a building site and worth a small fortune.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition comes from Manchester, a city famous for its music scene. Antiques expert Caroline Hawley finds an autograph from one of rock 'n' roll's biggest names, and Anita Manning values a beautiful concertina. Paul Martin takes a journey through the city's musical history, from the Halle Orchestra to New Order and Oasis.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, four previous players who came close to winning but never quite made it - Gethin Jones, Tiff Stevenson, Kate Thornton and Gary Wilmot - take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, four previous players who came close to winning but never quite made it - Gethin Jones, Tiff Stevenson, Kate Thornton and Gary Wilmot - take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: Nawal al Maghafi journeys across Iran to areas rarely accessed by international journalists, speaking to Iranians across the political and social divide about the impact of the war, and what comes next. Also, BBC Eye meets the motorcycle riders who risk their lives to smuggle Iranian fuel across the mountains into Pakistan. The BBC's senior international correspondent Nawal Al Maghafi is reporting from Iran on condition that none of her material is used on the BBC's Persian Service. These restrictions apply to all international media organisations operating in Iran.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders face the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. Clive Myrie hosts the classic quiz where contenders take to the black chair. The specialist subjects include British birds of prey, Roger Moore's tenure as James Bond, King Charles I and the American writer Sylvia Plath.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. A line-up formed from the members of rival quiz teams takes on three Douglas Adams fans, trying to establish the connection between four apparently random clues. For example: any light, see copy, peaty blonde and Effie Maiden – what connects them?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The Guildhall School of Music and Drama makes its University Challenge debut against Darwin College, Cambridge. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the dolphin get so smart? Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. Inside each one lies the result of a three-billion-year journey, from light-sensing cells to conscious thought.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: It’s the start of the coarse fishing season, and to celebrate Paul and Bob are in the Norfolk Broads to fish in some of East Anglia’s most historic and celebrated waterways. They’re here to try for rudd - but who knows what other species they might catch in these rivers, which are rich in flora and fauna? As is the way with a trip to the Broads, Paul and Bob do away with the car and instead get around by boat. It’s the quintessential Broads experience, although Paul does wonder whether he should have been captain instead of Bob...

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Sing Sing
programme.desc: Divine G, a man imprisoned at Sing Sing for a crime he did not commit, finds purpose and the strength to overcome the reality of prison life when he joins a drama group along with other inmates.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Ruby and Jodi’s partnership deepens as together they reshape the family, and Ruby starts to banish members of the family from their home.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Peter, now in his twenties, has been rearing Berkshire pigs since he was ten. He last competed at the Staffordshire County Show when he was 14. Having balanced university with work on the family farm in the Peak District, he wants to forge a future in farming. If his prized Berkshire pigs win rosettes in the competition ring, it will be not just recognition for him but also a much-needed boost for the breed, one of the rarest and oldest in the UK. While Peter hopes his pigs don’t give him the runaround, dedicated farming couple Lianne and Mark are working hard to grow their pedigree herd of South Devon cattle on rented land near Leek in Staffordshire. They are focused on giving their cows the ultimate beauty treatment so they shine in the show ring. South Devon cattle may be known as gentle giants, but overnighting at the showground, keeping up their energy levels and performing well in front of the judge are just some of the challenges they face to add more hard-earned rosettes to their collection.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: By invitation of the Lord Mayor of the City of London, the Roadshow visits the Mansion House, where Michael Aspel and the experts find both genuine and fake French art glass, a lock of Nelson's hair passed down from his hairdresser, a hand sculpted by Rodin and a broken plate dug up on a building site and worth a small fortune.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition comes from Manchester, a city famous for its music scene. Antiques expert Caroline Hawley finds an autograph from one of rock 'n' roll's biggest names, and Anita Manning values a beautiful concertina. Paul Martin takes a journey through the city's musical history, from the Halle Orchestra to New Order and Oasis.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, four previous players who came close to winning but never quite made it - Gethin Jones, Tiff Stevenson, Kate Thornton and Gary Wilmot - take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: Nawal al Maghafi journeys across Iran to areas rarely accessed by international journalists, speaking to Iranians across the political and social divide about the impact of the war, and what comes next. Also, BBC Eye meets the motorcycle riders who risk their lives to smuggle Iranian fuel across the mountains into Pakistan. The BBC's senior international correspondent Nawal Al Maghafi is reporting from Iran on condition that none of her material is used on the BBC's Persian Service. These restrictions apply to all international media organisations operating in Iran.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders face the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. Clive Myrie hosts the classic quiz where contenders take to the black chair. The specialist subjects include British birds of prey, Roger Moore's tenure as James Bond, King Charles I and the American writer Sylvia Plath.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. A line-up formed from the members of rival quiz teams takes on three Douglas Adams fans, trying to establish the connection between four apparently random clues. For example: any light, see copy, peaty blonde and Effie Maiden – what connects them?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The Guildhall School of Music and Drama makes its University Challenge debut against Darwin College, Cambridge. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the dolphin get so smart? Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. Inside each one lies the result of a three-billion-year journey, from light-sensing cells to conscious thought.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: It’s the start of the coarse fishing season, and to celebrate Paul and Bob are in the Norfolk Broads to fish in some of East Anglia’s most historic and celebrated waterways. They’re here to try for rudd - but who knows what other species they might catch in these rivers, which are rich in flora and fauna? As is the way with a trip to the Broads, Paul and Bob do away with the car and instead get around by boat. It’s the quintessential Broads experience, although Paul does wonder whether he should have been captain instead of Bob...

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Sing Sing
programme.desc: Divine G, a man imprisoned at Sing Sing for a crime he did not commit, finds purpose and the strength to overcome the reality of prison life when he joins a drama group along with other inmates.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Ruby and Jodi’s partnership deepens as together they reshape the family, and Ruby starts to banish members of the family from their home.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is in Buckinghamshire, determined to stop quality items being crushed at High Wycombe recycling centre. Three old chairs bring tears to the eyes, furniture upcycler Sarah dreams up a wild new look for a side table, and Jacqui's imagination is on fire as she wrestles a plant stand - but will all three items produce profits for their unsuspecting owners?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Suzie fixes a football from a Scottish Cup final, Chris repairs a magazine from a Japanese POW camp, Geoff restores a pachinko machine, and Rebecca fixes a beautiful Cretan lyra.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Sean Fletcher, Louise Minchin, Chris Washington and Kimberly Wyatt take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay hosts this quiz celebrating the UK and all its quirks. Alongside him, Traitors star Paul Gorton acts as an unreliable guide, leading a daily tour packed with fun, facts and fibs. This week’s celebrity contestants are TV icon Anneka Rice, comedian Shane Todd and Radio 1Xtra DJ Remi Burgz. The week kicks off in Whitby, with a daily winner and scores building up to eventually reveal a weekly champion.

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: It's the sixth leg of the Hairy Bikers' adventure and they have made it as far as southern Europe, Italy to be precise. Starting in Venice, the Bikers have to abandon their bikes in favour of a more elegant form of transport, the gondola, but that doesn't stop them cooking. By the side of a canal, they bake a classic focaccia with rosemary. But it's not long before they are back on the road, making a dash for Turin to help celebrate Italy's 150th birthday. In between, they cook a stromboli (American-style rolled-up pizza) and visit a hazelnut farm to learn the secrets of a certain hazelnut and chocolate spread. But it's off the beaten track that they enjoy the 'real Italy'; a pasta pie on the back streets of Ferrara, catching up with Si's sister who lives in Tuscany, visiting old friends at their weekend retreat for a Tuscan feast and the chance to relive The Italian Job on the rooftop track of the old Fiat factory. By the side of a canal, they bake a classic focaccia with rosemary. But it's not long before they are back on the road, making a dash for Turin to help celebrate Italy's 150th birthday. In between, they cook a stromboli (American-style rolled-up pizza) and visit a hazelnut farm to learn the secrets of a certain hazelnut and chocolate spread. But it's off the beaten track that they enjoy the 'real Italy'; a pasta pie on the back streets of Ferrara, catching up with Si's sister who lives in Tuscany, visiting old friends at their weekend retreat for a Tuscan feast and the chance to relive The Italian Job on the rooftop track of the old Fiat factory. World-class food, stunning scenery and fantastic people!

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Peter, now in his twenties, has been rearing Berkshire pigs since he was ten. He last competed at the Staffordshire County Show when he was 14. Having balanced university with work on the family farm in the Peak District, he wants to forge a future in farming. If his prized Berkshire pigs win rosettes in the competition ring, it will be not just recognition for him but also a much-needed boost for the breed, one of the rarest and oldest in the UK. While Peter hopes his pigs don’t give him the runaround, dedicated farming couple Lianne and Mark are working hard to grow their pedigree herd of South Devon cattle on rented land near Leek in Staffordshire. They are focused on giving their cows the ultimate beauty treatment so they shine in the show ring. South Devon cattle may be known as gentle giants, but overnighting at the showground, keeping up their energy levels and performing well in front of the judge are just some of the challenges they face to add more hard-earned rosettes to their collection.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: By invitation of the Lord Mayor of the City of London, the Roadshow visits the Mansion House, where Michael Aspel and the experts find both genuine and fake French art glass, a lock of Nelson's hair passed down from his hairdresser, a hand sculpted by Rodin and a broken plate dug up on a building site and worth a small fortune.

programme.title: Evolution

Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: It’s the start of the coarse fishing season, and to celebrate Paul and Bob are in the Norfolk Broads to fish in some of East Anglia’s most historic and celebrated waterways. They’re here to try for rudd - but who knows what other species they might catch in these rivers, which are rich in flora and fauna? As is the way with a trip to the Broads, Paul and Bob do away with the car and instead get around by boat. It’s the quintessential Broads experience, although Paul does wonder whether he should have been captain instead of Bob...

programme.title: Sing Sing

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is in Buckinghamshire, determined to stop quality items being crushed at High Wycombe recycling centre. programme.desc: The Winx face their toughest physical exam yet, pushing their magic and teamwork to the limits. Meanwhile, Bloom attempts to bond with the mysterious Damien.

programme.title: Bro's in Control
programme.desc: The bros are on a rescue mission to save a giant rubber duck while captaining a raft and a paddleboard. And the Lewis Sisters help take some selfies!

programme.title: So Awkward
programme.desc: Inspired by hit daytime TV shows, Lily plays cupid for Samson and Ulrika, Seb helps Jeff surprise Meg with an office makeover, and Frankie creates an art therapy trail.

programme.title: Malory Towers
programme.desc: When Felicity and Darrell debate that the Third should have the same freedoms as the Sixth, the sisters end up in a personal argument. Meanwhile, Gwen’s attempt at matronly duties ends in chaos.

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC
programme.desc: As a documentary crew follow their every move, can Hawx United win the Global Youth Cup?

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: 'Pando went to sleep in my bed and I didn't like that 'cos it's mine.' Bing and Pando are both tired but insist on one last game of hide-and-seek before bed. Pando finds a great hiding place under the covers of Bing's bed, but by the time Bing finds him he is fast asleep. Bing is tired too and gets upset when he thinks there is nowhere left for him to sleep, but Flop and Padget find a solution.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: When it's time for the Tubby Custard Ride, there's a special trailer the Teletubbies haven't seen before. It's for the Noo-Noo, who gets to go on a special Tubby Custard Ride.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Explore the amazing world around us with baby monkey Tee and his Mum, Mo. Sing along, join in with stories and get ready for some family fun!

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Welcome to Purple’s mixing factory, where he mixes two colours to create a new colour.
